problem: For the function $f(x,y,z)=z({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})^{-1/2},$ find the equation of the level surface $f(x,y,z)=1.$
worked_solution:
The level surfaces for the function $f(x,y,z)$ are given by the equation

$$
f(x,y,z)=c.
$$

In our case, we're interested in $c=1.$ So, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =c \\ z({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})^{-1/2} & =1 \\ z & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the level surface for $c=1$ is the surface $z=\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}.$
